title: Heritage sites in Puducherry: White Town, Arikamedu and temples
seo_title: Heritage Sites in Puducherry: White Town, Arikamedu, Temples
meta_description: Heritage sites in Puducherry: the French White Town, the Tamil Quarter, Arikamedu's Indo-Roman port, Villianur and Bahur temples, and Karaikal and Mahe.
summary: Puducherry's heritage runs from Arikamedu, an Indo-Roman trading port of around the 2nd century BCE to 2nd century CE, through Chola-period temples at Bahur, Villianur and Thirubuvanai, to the planned French colonial town of the 18th century with its grid of streets, Tamil and French quarters, churches and the Pondicherry Museum. There is no UNESCO site.

paras: Puducherry was a coastal Tamil settlement long before the Europeans arrived. Arikamedu, just south of the town, shows it was trading with the Roman world around the turn of the common era. In the Chola period, temples with inscriptions were built in villages nearby. The French East India Company established Pondichéry in 1674, and it remained the capital of French India, with Karaikal, Mahe, Yanam and Chandannagar, until de facto transfer to India in 1954.

The result is a small territory where early historic trade, Tamil temple culture and French town planning sit within a few kilometres of each other. Our [Puducherry heritage walk guide](heritage-walk-in-puducherry.html) covers the town on foot.

Arikamedu, on the Ariyankuppam river, was excavated by French archaeologists in the 1940s and by Mortimer Wheeler in 1945, and later by Vimala Begley's team. It yielded Roman amphorae, Arretine ware, glass beads, rouletted ware and evidence of bead making and textile dyeing. It is the best known site for trade between the Tamil coast and the Mediterranean world.

Little is visible on the ground today beyond a ruined colonial building and the mound, so the finds in the Pondicherry Museum are the main way to see it. Our session [Foods as historical evidence: coconut, spice and exchange](foods-as-historical-evidence-coconut-spice-and-exchange.html) explains what such trade tells us, and [Clay and the past](clay-and-the-past-a-pottery-workshop.html) teaches students to recognise pottery types like those from Arikamedu.

The Thirukameshwarar temple at Villianur, with its large tank and gopuram, has Chola-period origins and later additions. The Moolanathar temple at Bahur carries Chola inscriptions, including references to a college of Vedic learning in the village. The Thirubuvanai temple has fine Chola sculpture. In town, the Manakula Vinayagar temple predates the French.

These temples suit students who want to see how inscriptions record gifts, land and learning. Our lecture [Temple inscriptions and patrons](temple-inscriptions-patrons.html) uses south Indian examples like Bahur.

sections.h2: The French town and the Tamil Quarter
paras: Puducherry's grid plan was laid out in the 18th century, with a canal dividing the European quarter by the sea, now called White Town, from the Tamil town inland. White Town has colonnaded mansions, the Raj Nivas (former Governor's palace), the French war memorial, the Église de Notre Dame des Anges and the seafront promenade. The Tamil Quarter has houses with verandahs (thinnais), carved wooden doors and courtyards.

The Sacred Heart Basilica, Immaculate Conception Cathedral and Sri Aurobindo Ashram are nearby. Our lecture on [cemeteries, epitaphs and public memory](cemeteries-epitaphs-and-public-memory.html) uses colonial towns like this one, and the Tamil Nadu coast including [Mahabalipuram](heritage-walk-in-mahabalipuram.html) is close enough for a combined trip.

sections.h2: Karaikal, Mahe and Yanam, and planning a visit
paras: The territory also includes Karaikal on the Tamil coast, Mahe on the Malabar coast in Kerala and Yanam in the Godavari delta in Andhra Pradesh, each with French-era buildings and churches. November to February is the most comfortable season.

We build a [study tour for your group](a-study-tour-built-for-your-group.html) that combines Puducherry with Mahabalipuram and the Chola temples, and our [South India temple architecture](south-india-temple-architecture.html) tour can start or finish here.

faq.a: Arikamedu, south of Puducherry, was a trading port linked to the Roman world around the 2nd century BCE to 2nd century CE. Excavations found Roman amphorae, Arretine ware, glass beads and bead-making waste. The finds are in the Pondicherry Museum.

faq.q: Are there UNESCO World Heritage Sites in Puducherry?
faq.a: No. Puducherry has no UNESCO World Heritage Site. Its heritage value lies in Arikamedu, the Chola-period temples nearby and the planned French colonial town.

faq.q: What is the difference between White Town and the Tamil Quarter?
faq.a: White Town is the former European quarter by the sea, with colonnaded mansions and churches. The Tamil Quarter, west of the old canal, has Tamil houses with verandahs, carved doors and courtyards. Both follow the 18th century grid plan.

faq.q: Which are the old temples near Puducherry?
faq.a: The Thirukameshwarar temple at Villianur, the Moolanathar temple at Bahur and the temple at Thirubuvanai all have Chola-period origins and inscriptions. In town, the Manakula Vinayagar temple is older than the French settlement.
